title.narrative: GAMBIA - READ: Results for Education Achievement and Development Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Results for Education Achievement and Development (READ) Project for Gambia is to increase access to basic education, improve quality of teaching and learning in lower basic schools, and strengthen education systems. The project has four components. The first component will support increasing access to basic education. It has following four sub-components: (i) school construction; (ii) donkey carts; (iii) community-based early childhood care and development (ECD); and (iv) provision of school sub-grants to support sub-projects to all lower and upper basic public schools and stationery to all students in lower basic education in hardship areas. The second component aims to improve quality of teaching and learning. It has following eight sub-components: (a) enhancing teacher training; (b) stipends for teacher students; (c) hardship allowances for public lower and upper basic teachers in remote areas; (d) extended teacher continuing professional development; (e) teacher supervision and support through the use of a standardized classroom observation tool; (f) reading in the early grades with a focus on building reading abilities; (g) reading in the early grades with a focus on building reading abilities; and (h) LEARNET, a public-private partnership (PPP) initiative for information and communication technology (ICT) integration in learning and teaching, will provide broadband and curriculum- linked dynamic e-content to public schools. The third component, technical assistance (TA) aims to support institutional and capacity strengthening interventions to facilitate the implementation of components one and two and engaging in effective communication regarding the sector and the READ project. It has following two sub-components: (i) development and implementation of a strong communication strategy including dissemination of information, training, outreach campaigns, and surveys; and (ii) institutional support and capacity building. The fourth component, strengthening the education system with a focus on governance and management results aims to improve access to education, and teachers and students' performance, through the achievement of disbursement linked indicators (DLIs).
To increase access to basic education, improve quality of teaching and learning in lower basic schools, and strengthen education systems.

title.narrative: Head Teachers in lower basic schools adjusting School Development Plans in response to NAT results and approved by Regional Directorates using an agreed upon check list

comment.narrative: Trainings on the School Development Plans (SDP) were conducted four times throughout the project by Standards and Quality Assurance Directorate (SQAD), Assessment Unit and Planning Directorate of MoBSE. 1. In Sep 2015, 800 head teachers and cluster monitors attened the training, 2. In January 2016, 230 head teachers who were not in the first training attended the training with the planning focal points and SQAD representative, 3. In April 2016, the second training was conducted for all head teachers, RED staff and cluster trainers, and 4. In June 2016, 200 head teachers and Planning Directorate's focal points attended a make up training to evaluate the SDP properly. In July 2018, third party consultants evaluated the SDPs and confirmed that 95.3 percent of SDP achieved the results.

Number of additional classrooms built or rehabilitated at the primary level resulting from project interventions.

comment.narrative: Achieved. Originally it was planned to build 40 multi-grade schools with two classrooms each. After the ECD impact evaluation, which revealed that children in the Annexed ECD (attached to LBS) learned more. Subsequently, the MoBSE decided to build more multi-grade schools with Annexed ECD, instead of 40 community-based ECD structures. The cost of 40 community-based ECD sheds equaled the two multi-grade schools with two LBS classrooms and one ECD classroom each.

Annual formal and informal school fees paid by parents to public lower basic schools

comment.narrative: Achieved. In 2016, a third party firm conducted the evaluation to see if parents are asked to pay annual formal and informal fees and confirmed that they are not paying fees anymore. A very small proportion (2.9%) of parents paid US$0.3 on average, which means that actual achieved at completion is US$0.009 against US$12 at the baseline.
